title: Current makes a magnetic field
target: Connect current direction with the magnetic field around a wire.
criteria: Sketch circular field lines around a straight wire.
Predict the effect of reversing current.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: Around a long straight current-carrying wire, what shape do magnetic field lines have?
options: Straight lines only along the wire.
No pattern until the wire touches a magnet.
cpa.guide: Symmetry gives circular magnetic field lines around the current.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: Two points are equally far from a long straight wire in a uniform surrounding material. What does the ideal model predict about field magnitude?
options: Zero at one point solely because it is left of the wire.
The field points radially outward at both.
Magnitude depends only on compass color.
cpa.guide: For the ideal straight wire, magnitude depends on current and radial distance, not angular position.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: Conventional current points into the page. Point your right thumb into the page. Which way do your curled fingers indicate the field?
cpa.guide: The right-hand grip rule gives clockwise circles for current into the page.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: Current points out of the page. At a point directly above the wire, which way is the magnetic field?
cpa.guide: Out-of-page current gives counterclockwise circles; the tangent at the top points left.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: The current through a straight wire reverses with unchanged magnitude. What happens to the field at a fixed point?
options: Direction reverses; magnitude stays the same.
Magnitude doubles; direction stays the same.
cpa.guide: Field direction follows current direction; magnitude depends on its absolute value.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: At a fixed distance from a straight wire, current changes from 2 A out of the page to 6 A into the page. Use B ∝ |I|. What changes?
options: Magnitude triples but direction stays the same.
Magnitude stays fixed and direction reverses.
Field magnitude triples and direction reverses.
Magnitude falls to one-third and direction reverses.
cpa.guide: The current magnitude increases by 3 and its sign reverses.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.
